title: He measured a country's progress by what its people could actually do - not just its GDP.

sources.text: Nobel Prize official site - Amartya Sen, Facts

caption:
He measured a country's progress by what its people could actually do - not just its GDP.

In 1998, he became the first Asian to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, awarded for his contributions to welfare economics.

That framework now underpins the Human Development Index and shapes how governments and economists worldwide think about growth that actually reaches people.

His insight - that development means expanding what people can actually do with their lives - is a quieter, harder standard than any single growth number.
